item.title: The U.S. names its 7th dead soldier and oil prices spike on Day 10 of the Iran war
item.summary: The Pentagon said a Space Brigade sergeant was killed and the price of oil increased after Iran named Mojtaba Khamenei as supreme leader and then launched new attacks at Israel and Gulf states.

item.title: World shares tumble as Iran war pushes crude prices over $110 a barrel
item.summary: World shares tumbled on Monday, with Japan's benchmark Nikkei 225 index plunging more than 5%, after oil prices spiked at nearly $120 a barrel.

item.title: Attempted attack with explosives in New York City investigated as "ISIS-inspired terrorism"
item.summary: New York City INYPD Commissioner: "Explosive devices that could have caused serious injury or death."

item.title: Live Nation and Justice Department reach settlement in antitrust case
item.summary: The trial, which began a week ago in a New York City courtroom, aimed to break up Live Nation and its subsidiary, Ticketmaster.

item.title: Trump is using immigration policy to suppress speech, lawsuit claims
item.summary: A new lawsuit accuses the administration of violating the First Amendment by threatening the visas of researchers for work on disinformation and content moderation of social media.

item.title: Why young girls are disguised as boys in Afghanistan
item.summary: The Taliban has released a video of an interrogation of a girl who passed as a boy. It's an age-old practice in this patriarchal society but now appears to be happening with some frequency.

item.title: Bill Kurtis retires as 'Wait Wait...Don't Tell Me!' judge and scorekeeper
item.summary: Legendary anchorman and America's favorite judge and scorekeeper, Bill Kurtis is retiring from his role at Wait Wait…Don't Tell Me!, capping off a phenomenal 12-year run with the show.

item.title: The next redistricting battle might be who is counted in state legislative districts
item.summary: A Republican push to alter the census may lead to a radical shift in redistricting for state legislatures — drawing districts that don't take into account children and non-U.S. citizen adults.

item.title: Chimps' taste for fermented fruit hints at the origins of humans' love of alcohol
item.summary: Scientists analyzed the urine of wild chimpanzees who'd feasted on fallen fruit to see how much alcohol they consumed from the fermented sugars.

item.title: Come along with some geese as they migrate back from their southern winter havens
item.summary: Geese's iconic "V" formations and trademark squawks can be seen and heard overhead as they go back and forth to the south through the year. But what does it take for such a long trip?
